title: Dengue with warning signs, 24-year-old man
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Fever for 4 days with abdominal pain and vomiting 4 times today; feeling lethargic.
intake.history: Neighbour diagnosed with dengue last week. Gum bleeding this morning.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 2. A: DENGUE, SUSPECTED row p8, Level 2 column (x~131): 'Fever onset 3 - 6 days' (day 4), 'Lethargy / Near-fainting' (lethargic), 'SBP < HR' (104 < 108) and 'SBP - DBP < 30' (104-80 = 24) all apply. Level 3 cells (x~244) also apply ('Abdominal pain', 'Persistent vomiting', HR 100-120, Temp 37.5-39, pain 4-7), and gum bleeding is 'ENT Bleeding', Level 3 in primary triage (p5 x~356). Most urgent = Level 2. No adult Level 1 shock cell is documented (cold peripheries, absent radial pulse and severe tachycardia are not recorded). B: The 'Dengue, suspected' complaint row (adult, p8) gives Level 2 (x~131) for 'Fever onset 3 - 6 days', 'Lethargy / Near-fainting', 'SBP < HR' and 'SBP - DBP < 30'. This patient has fever on day 4, lethargy, SBP 104 < HR 108 and pulse pressure 24, so all four apply. Abdominal pain and persistent vomiting alone would be Level 3 (x~244). Vital signs: HR 108 and Temp 37.8 are Level 3 (p7, x~244); pain 5 is Level 3.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Compensated shock or not: the intake has HR 108, BP 104/80 (pulse pressure 24, raised diastolic) and lethargy, but no CRT or extremity temperature. The CPG's Table 1 compensated-shock features partly fit. Preferred disposition is ADMIT_WARD with HDU acceptable; adjudicator may prefer HDU.

NSAID/steroid/injection prohibitions come from the CPG's patient home-care leaflet (Appendix 9), not the clinician recommendations; no clinician-facing sentence in the adult CPG explicitly bans NSAIDs.
The graded fluid bolus (Table 8) is for 'persistent warning signs with increasing or persistently high HCT'; HCT is not yet known at triage.
B: Whether he is already in compensated shock is borderline. Tachycardia above SBP, raised diastolic (80) with pulse pressure 24, and lethargy match the compensated-shock column of Table 1, but CRT and extremity temperature are not recorded. I labelled the primary diagnosis 'with warning signs' and put compensated shock as an acceptable alternative and a red flag.

The adult CPG says 'avoid NSAIDs/steroids/injections' only in the patient Home Care Leaflet (Appendix 9); the clinician chapters give no explicit prohibition. The paediatric CPG's 'Do not prescribe ... NSAIDs or intramuscular injections' is the clearer statement, but it is for children.
